source.citation: van der Lugt, G. (Ed.). (2016). Nutrient Solutions for Greenhouse Crops. Joint initiative of AkzoNobel, Eurofins Agro, NMI, SQM and YARA.
source.lineage: Preface (PDF7) states the data are mainly based on the 1999 Naaldwijk (PBG) research material, with several values revised from later field experience.
source.locator_convention: Crop tables are unnumbered; cite file + PDF page + printed page + crop/substrate heading + column name.

units.note: Macro and micro units differ. Never convert between mmol/L, me/L and mg/L without the ion valence and molar mass.

cucumber.locator: out/eurofins_nutrient_solutions.pdf PDF41 / printed 41, 'CROP: CUCUMBER (Cucumis sativus) - INERT SUBSTRATE'

root_zone_targets.note: Root-zone analysis targets, not the feed.

adjustment_notes.blank_cells: A blank printed cell is 'no adjustment stated', not a measured zero.
adjustment_notes.fruit_set_ca: The cucumber Fruit Set Ca cell is printed blank while the footnote gives a range of 0.2-0.75 mmol/L for Ca. Direction and default cannot be resolved from the source; left null on purpose.
adjustment_notes.footnote_range: Footnote *: adjustments for fruit set may vary 0.25-2 mmol/L for K and 0.2-0.75 mmol/L for Ca.
adjustment_notes.high_water_trigger: Footnote **: recommended when water supply exceeds 5 L/m2/day.
adjustment_notes.end_season_definition: Footnote ***: growing point removed, usually autumn, vine no longer extends and the last fruits ripen.
adjustment_notes.ec_ph: No numeric EC or pH adjustment is printed for any stage.

worked_stock_example.basis: Computed by the source from the uncorrected base solution (PDF39 note); not stage/raw-water/drain corrected.

tomato.locator: out/eurofins_nutrient_solutions.pdf PDF56 / printed 56, 'CROP: TOMATO (Solanum lycopersicum) - INERT SUBSTRATE'

root_zone_targets.note: The two <0.05 values are printed as such; PDF29 prints NH4 <0.5 and Cl <6.0 for tomato drain. Preserved as a source inconsistency.

adjustment_notes.blank_cells: A blank printed cell is 'no adjustment stated', not a measured zero.
adjustment_notes.footnote_range: Footnote *: adjustments for fruit set may vary 0.25-2 mmol/L for K and 0.2-0.75 mmol/L for Ca.
adjustment_notes.high_water_trigger: Footnote **: recommended when water supply exceeds 5 L/m2/day.
adjustment_notes.end_season_definition: The cucumber autumn/end-of-crop footnote is not repeated on the tomato page.
adjustment_notes.ec_ph: No numeric EC or pH adjustment is printed for any stage.

worked_stock_example.basis: Computed by the source from the uncorrected base solution (PDF39 note); not stage/raw-water/drain corrected.

season_axis.finding: The source has no spring/summer/autumn/winter composition table, no monthly table and no radiation-based EC formula for tomato or cucumber. Summer/Winter columns exist only for lettuce (PDF64) and roses (PDF78-79) and must not be transferred to these crops.
what_the_source_does_offer: High water: a water-supply regime, triggered above 5 L/m2/day (PDF41, PDF56 footnote **).
End season: cucumber growing point removed, usually autumn (PDF41 footnote ***).
PDF23 step 3 states concentrations are adjusted for growth stage or seasonal effects, without a table.
PDF22 states relatively more Ca early and relatively more K from flowering and fruit development.
season_axis.implication: Season enters this source through water uptake rate and crop stage, not through a separate seasonal recipe. Do not synthesize monthly recipes from it.

normalization.reference_ec: Reference EC is generally 0.3 mS/cm below the target EC [PDF21].
normalization.excluded: Na and HCO3 are not normalized. Cl is normalized only when it is in the target list.

drain_correction.not_published: Per-ion correction factors are deliberately omitted by the source because they depend on local conditions (PDF22). No damping constant, no cumulative cap, no re-measurement interval is given.
drain_correction.feed_ec_change_exception: When macronutrients are scaled to reach a required feed EC, NH4, P, Fe and the other micronutrients are NOT scaled [PDF23 step 4].
drain_correction.calculation_order: Stage/analysis correction -> subtract raw-water nutrients -> subtract the drain nutrients corresponding to the reused drain volume -> restore cation/anion balance [PDF23 steps 5-7].
drain_correction.ion_balance: Eq cations = NH4 + K + Na + 2*Ca + 2*Mg ; Eq anions = NO3 + Cl + 2*SO4 + HCO3 + H2PO4. A difference under about 10% is practically acceptable [PDF21].
drain_correction.iron_exception: Do not subtract non-chelated raw-water Fe from the chelated Fe dose; calculate chelated Fe separately [PDF13].
drain_correction.disinfection: UV/ozone drain disinfection partly degrades chelates; add chelate replenishment after disinfection [PDF35]. No quantitative rate is given.

sodium.raw_water_limit: Raw water above 1.5 mmol/L Na is generally unsuitable for recirculation [PDF11].
sodium.chloride_rule: Cl maximum is stated as 0.2-0.5 mmol/L above the Na maximum [PDF12].
sodium.action: Discharge part of the recirculating solution when Na exceeds the crop maximum. No discharge fraction or formula is given.

drain_correction.drain_fraction: No numeric drain-fraction target and no drain/feed EC difference target is published for tomato or cucumber in this source.
drain_correction.worked_example_warning: PDF29 'Example report Drainwater Tomato - Recirculation' prints per-ion Correction values (K -0.5, Ca -0.5, P -0.3, Fe +13, Zn +2.5, B +7.5, Cu -0.2) but it is one example report, not a general coefficient set, and its Basic scheme uses Fe 25 umol/L against the crop page's 15.

stock_tank_rules.standard: Standard concentration factor 100; tanks A and B of 1000 L (1 m3) each, feeding 100,000 L (100 m3) of working solution [PDF31].
stock_tank_rules.separation: All calcium fertilizers in A, all phosphate and sulphate fertilizers in B, to prevent precipitation.
stock_tank_rules.splittable: Potassium nitrate, magnesium nitrate, ammonium nitrate and nitric acid may be divided over both tanks to balance the dissolved load.
stock_tank_rules.micronutrients: Sulphate micronutrients go in B; chelates may go in either, preferably A when much acid is used.
stock_tank_rules.acid: Only a few litres of acid per m3 in A; the remainder in B.
stock_tank_rules.filling: Fill to about 3/4 with water, add fertilizers one at a time with continuous stirring, top up after the macro salts dissolve, check pH, then add micronutrients.
stock_tank_rules.ph: Tank B below pH 5; tank A pH 3.5-5. The source is internally inconsistent about the 3.5 boundary (PDF31 vs PDF36).
stock_tank_rules.solubility: The source publishes no per-salt solubility limit table. PDF26 Table 5 lists formulas, element percentages, molar masses and liquid densities only.

acid_and_bicarbonate.residual: Leave 0.5-0.75 mmol/L HCO3 in the feed to buffer pH near 5.5-6; full neutralization can drop pH below 5 [PDF24].
acid_and_bicarbonate.acid_choice: Nitric acid is usual; phosphoric acid and urea phosphate are possible. Nitrate or phosphate from the acid must not push the feed above target [PDF13].
acid_and_bicarbonate.degassing: React in an open mixing tank so the CO2 produced can escape [PDF13].
acid_and_bicarbonate.ph_via_ammonium: Root-zone pH too low: NH4 0-0.5 mmol/L; too high: up to 1.5 mmol/L [PDF16].

known_source_inconsistencies: Tomato feed Fe 15 umol/L (PDF56) vs 25 umol/L in the PDF29 drain example Basic scheme.
Cucumber Na <6 mmol/L printed with <184 ppm (PDF41) vs 6 mmol/L / 138 ppm (PDF12 Table 2).
Tomato Cu 0.75 umol/L / 48 ppb (PDF56) vs 0.8 umol/L / 50 ppb (PDF34 Table 6).
Tomato B 30 umol/L printed as 324 ppb (PDF56) vs 330 ppb (PDF34 Table 6).
Cucumber ORGANIC MATERIAL page prints target EC 1.4 and 3 mS/cm on the same table (PDF42); tomato prints 1.5 and 1.4 (PDF57).
Cucumber Fruit Set Ca cell blank while the footnote gives a 0.2-0.75 mmol/L range.
Chelate stability pH boundary stated as 'pH 3.5 or lower' degrades, tank A allowed 3.5-5 (PDF31), and 'above 3.5' (PDF36).
